questions.question_text: A standing passenger tends to fall backward when a bus starts suddenly. Which explanation best accounts for the motion?
questions.option_a: The passenger's body tends to remain at rest due to inertia
questions.option_c: The bus pulls the passenger backward with a magnetic force
questions.explanation: When the bus accelerates forward, the passenger's lower body moves with it while the upper body tends to remain at rest, producing the backward lean.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Force and Laws of Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A car takes much longer to stop on a wet road than on a dry road at the same initial speed. The most direct reason is that wet conditions can reduce
questions.option_c: the normal force of Earth on the car to zero
questions.explanation: Reduced tyre-road friction limits the braking force, so the car needs more distance and time to stop.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Force and Laws of Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A loaded truck and an empty car are both moving at the same speed. Which one has greater linear momentum?
questions.option_a: The loaded truck, because it has greater mass
questions.option_b: The empty car, because it has smaller mass
questions.option_c: They have equal momentum because their speeds match
questions.option_d: Neither has momentum until it accelerates
questions.explanation: Momentum p = mv. At the same speed, the object with greater mass has greater momentum.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Force and Laws of Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A 4 kg object experiences a net force of 12 N. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives a = F/m = 12/4 = 3 m/s².
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Force and Laws of Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The same net force is applied separately to a 2 kg body and a 6 kg body. How do their accelerations compare?
questions.option_a: The 2 kg body accelerates three times as much
questions.option_b: The 6 kg body accelerates three times as much
questions.explanation: For fixed force, a = F/m; reducing mass from 6 kg to 2 kg triples acceleration.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Force and Laws of Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A 0.20 kg ball moves east at 10 m/s and is returned west at 5 m/s. Taking east as positive, what is the ball's change in momentum?
questions.explanation: Initial p = +2.0 kg·m/s and final p = −1.0 kg·m/s, so Δp = −1.0 − 2.0 = −3.0 kg·m/s.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Force and Laws of Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A 0.15 kg cricket ball moving at 20 m/s has what momentum?
questions.explanation: Momentum is mass times velocity: 0.15 × 20 = 3 kg·m/s in the direction of motion.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Force and Laws of Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why does an airbag reduce the force on a passenger during a collision if the passenger's momentum change is similar?
questions.option_a: It increases the time over which the momentum changes
questions.explanation: For a given momentum change, a longer stopping time lowers average force because FΔt = Δp.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A gun recoils backward when a bullet is fired forward. If external forces are negligible during the brief firing interval, the recoil follows from conservation of
questions.explanation: The bullet's forward momentum is balanced by backward momentum of the gun so the system's total momentum remains approximately conserved.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Force and Laws of Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A rocket accelerates in space by ejecting exhaust gas backward. The forward thrust is explained primarily by
questions.option_a: Newton's third law and conservation of momentum
questions.option_c: air pushing on the rocket from behind
questions.explanation: The rocket pushes exhaust backward; the exhaust exerts an equal and opposite force on the rocket, and momentum is conserved for the system.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A block at rest on a rough incline tends to slide down the slope. In which direction does static friction on the block act?
questions.option_d: It must be zero for a block at rest
questions.explanation: Static friction opposes the impending relative motion; if the block tends to slide down, friction acts up the plane.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A book rests on a table. The book's weight and the table's normal force do not form a Newton's third-law pair because they
questions.option_a: both act on the same object
questions.option_d: act only when the book moves
questions.explanation: The weight and normal force both act on the book and balance; third-law partners act on different bodies (Earth on book and book on Earth, or table on book and book on table).
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Force and Laws of Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A car moves north while slowing down on a straight road. In which direction is its acceleration?
questions.option_d: Zero, because it is still moving north
questions.explanation: Acceleration points in the direction of velocity change. A reduction in northward speed is a southward change in velocity.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: For an object moving uniformly around a circle, the centripetal acceleration points
questions.option_a: toward the centre of the circle
questions.option_b: tangentially in the direction of motion
questions.option_d: opposite to gravity in every case
questions.explanation: The inward centripetal acceleration continually changes the direction of velocity and is directed toward the centre.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A stone tied to a string moves in a circle. If the string suddenly breaks, the stone initially travels approximately
questions.option_a: along the tangent to the circular path
questions.explanation: At the instant the centripetal constraint disappears, the stone continues with its instantaneous tangential velocity, neglecting other forces.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A 1,000 kg car moves at 10 m/s around a curve of radius 50 m. What centripetal force is required?
questions.explanation: F = mv²/r = 1,000 × 100/50 = 2,000 N, directed toward the centre of the curve.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A velocity-time graph is a straight line with a constant positive slope. The slope represents
questions.explanation: The slope of a velocity-time graph is change in velocity per unit time, which is acceleration.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The area under a velocity-time graph over a time interval gives the object's
questions.explanation: Integrating velocity with respect to time gives displacement; area below the axis contributes negative displacement.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A position-time graph is horizontal for a moving observer's reference frame. What does this indicate about the object's motion?
questions.option_a: Its position is constant, so it is at rest in that frame
questions.option_d: It is moving in a circle
questions.explanation: A horizontal position-time graph has zero slope, hence zero velocity relative to that reference frame.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A car covers 120 km in 2 hours, stops for 1 hour, then covers another 60 km in 1 hour. What is its average speed for the whole trip?
questions.explanation: Total distance is 180 km and total elapsed time including the stop is 4 h; average speed is 180/4 = 45 km/h.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A runner completes one full 400 m lap and ends where they started. Which statement is correct for the completed lap?
questions.option_a: Distance is 400 m and displacement is zero
questions.option_b: Distance is zero and displacement is 400 m
questions.option_c: Both distance and displacement are 400 m
questions.option_d: Both distance and displacement are zero
questions.explanation: Distance counts the path travelled; displacement is the directed change from starting to ending position, which is zero after a full lap.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A force-time graph is a rectangle of height 6 N and width 0.5 s. What momentum change does it represent?
questions.explanation: Impulse equals area under the force-time graph: 6 × 0.5 = 3 N·s, equal to change in momentum.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Two forces of 12 N east and 5 N west act on an object along the same line. What is the net force?
questions.explanation: Opposite collinear forces subtract: 12 − 5 = 7 N in the direction of the larger force, east.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Force and Laws of Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A bus travels at constant velocity on a straight, level road. Which statement about the net force on it is correct?
questions.option_b: The net force must point forward
questions.option_c: The net force must point backward
questions.option_d: A non-zero net force is required to maintain constant velocity
questions.explanation: Constant velocity means zero acceleration, so the resultant force is zero; individual forces such as thrust and resistance can still act and balance.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Force and Laws of Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A 5 kg block rests on a horizontal table with no other vertical forces. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is the table’s normal force on it?
questions.explanation: There is no vertical acceleration, so the upward normal force balances the block’s weight: N = mg = 5×10 = 50 N.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Force and Laws of Motion, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Two cars travel in the same direction at 25 m/s and 15 m/s. What is the speed of the faster car relative to the slower one?
questions.explanation: For motion in the same direction, relative speed is the difference: 25 − 15 = 10 m/s.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Motion and Force, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A 3 N force acts east and a 4 N force acts north on an object. What is the magnitude of the resultant force?
questions.explanation: The forces are perpendicular, so the resultant magnitude is √(3²+4²) = 5 N.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Motion and Force, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A box remains at rest while a 20 N horizontal force is applied. The maximum available static friction is 30 N. What friction force acts on the box?
questions.explanation: Static friction adjusts to balance the applied force up to its maximum; here it is 20 N, not automatically 30 N.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Motion and Force, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A car brakes with constant deceleration on a level road. If its initial speed is doubled while the braking deceleration remains the same, how does the stopping distance change?
questions.option_a: It becomes four times as large
questions.explanation: From v² = u² + 2as with final speed zero, stopping distance is proportional to the square of initial speed when deceleration is fixed.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Motion and Force, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
